anatomy.flutter: Kbd(text) builds a Surface(fill: theme.muted, radius: Radii.sm) > Padding(px-1) > Center(widthFactor:1) > StyledText(TextStyles.code), wrapped in ConstrainedBox(minWidth/minHeight: space(5)) then IgnorePointer(SelectionContainer.disabled(...)); KbdGroup(children) is a MergeSemantics(Row) of Kbd widgets.
anatomy.web: <kbd data-slot="kbd"> carries the whole class list itself (min-h-5 w-fit min-w-5 rounded-sm bg-muted px-1 font-sans text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground) as one flat element; <kbd data-slot="kbd-group"> (KbdGroup) wraps children the same way — both are single leaf elements rather than a composed widget tree, but express the identical box model.

api.flutter: Kbd(this.text) takes exactly one required String — the legend — per the doc comment: 'Takes the key's legend as a string, because that is all the page ever passes it'; KbdGroup(children) takes a List<Widget> of Kbd instances.
api.web: Kbd is React.ComponentProps<"kbd"> — a thin passthrough where children is typically a bare string ('Ctrl', 'K'); KbdGroup is React.ComponentProps<"div"> despite rendering a <kbd> element (documented drift 19), also holding a list of Kbd children.

states.flutter: Kbd is a StatelessWidget with no interactive state — IgnorePointer makes it inert to the mouse, matching pointer-events-none, and there is no hover/focus/pressed/disabled branch anywhere in kbd.dart.
states.web: Kbd's class list is entirely static except for the ambient `in-data-[slot=tooltip-content]:` recolor variant (a context-driven repaint, not an interaction state) — pointer-events-none and select-none make it as inert on the web as IgnorePointer + SelectionContainer.disabled make it in Flutter.
states.note: Kbd is a decorative label with no rest/hover/focus/pressed/loading/disabled matrix on either platform — pointer-events-none/IgnorePointer specifically ensures it never enters any of those states, so the dimension does not apply.

disabled.flutter: No `enabled`/`disabled` concept exists in kbd.dart — Kbd always renders the same way regardless of any ancestor's disabled state.
disabled.web: Kbd has no disabled: variant in its class list either — it is a passive label, not a control, so there is nothing to disable.
disabled.note: A keyboard-shortcut legend is not itself operable on either platform, so neither side has (or needs) a disabled path.

interaction.flutter: IgnorePointer wraps the whole key so no gesture ever reaches it, and SelectionContainer.disabled prevents text selection — reproducing pointer-events-none and select-none exactly; there is no focus/keyboard handling because Kbd is not a control.
interaction.web: pointer-events-none and select-none on the <kbd> element itself produce the identical inert-to-mouse, non-selectable behaviour; a <kbd> element has no default keyboard interaction either.

semantics.flutter: KbdGroup wraps its Row in MergeSemantics specifically so 'Ctrl' + 'K' announce as one merged node ('Ctrl K') rather than two separate keys, per the doc comment's explicit reasoning about the web's nested-<kbd> markup meaning one keyboard object.
semantics.web: KbdGroup renders <kbd><kbd>Ctrl</kbd><kbd>K</kbd></kbd> (documented drift 19: the component is typed as a div but renders a kbd) — a real nested <kbd>, which a screen reader reads as one shortcut string because kbd carries no distinct accessible role of its own; MergeSemantics is the correct Flutter translation of that same reading, not a literal DOM reproduction (which Flutter has no element name to get 'wrong' in the first place).
